people.Short bio (card) *: Leads both groups: extragalactic astronomy and observational cosmology in SEA OtTeRS, precision instrumentation in SEAL Lab.
people.Long bio (profile page):
Krittapas (Bright) Chanchaiworawit is an extragalactic astrophysicist and instrument builder at the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT), where he leads two research groups: SEA OtTeRS, an extragalactic astronomy and time-domain group that operates its own low-resolution spectrographs on the Thai National Telescope (TNT) and the Thai Robotic Telescopes (TRT), and SEAL Lab, Thailand's first ultra-precision single-point diamond-turning laboratory for astronomical and space optics.

His research asks how galaxies, their central black holes, and their environments assemble and interact across cosmic time: how large-scale structure formation influences or quenches star formation at high redshift toward the epoch of first assembly and reionization, and how supermassive black holes grow and co-evolve with their host galaxies, studied through time-domain monitoring of AGN variability. He initiated NARIT's simulation work for ESA's ARRAKIHS mission and serves as the institute's liaison to the mission consortium.

He holds a BS in Physics from Lehigh University (2012) and an MS (2014) and PhD in Astronomy (2018) from the University of Florida, where his dissertation reported the discovery of the highest-redshift protocluster of Lyman-α emitters at z = 6.5. He was a Postdoctoral Associate at the University of Florida (2018–2019) and a Postdoctoral Fellow at Florida Atlantic University (2019–2021) before joining NARIT as a Researcher in 2021.

projects.Project name *: Compact Low-Resolution Spectrograph for the 0.7-m Thai Robotic Telescopes
projects.One-line summary *: Single long-slit spectrograph with dichroic-split iz-band guiding for fully robotic transient classification and AGN reverberation monitoring on the 0.7-m TRT.
projects.Description: Commissioned on the 0.7-m Thai Robotic Telescope at NARIT AstroPark, with first light on Jan 27, 2025. Its on-sky performance and image quality were published at SPIE 2025 and 2026, with the optomechanical design and upgraded mechanical components described in companion proceedings.

projects.Project name *: SPDT Engineering, Assembly, and Laser Metrology Laboratory
projects.One-line summary *: Thailand's first ultra-precision reflective-surface laboratory: 5-axis single-point diamond turning, surface metrology, and a complete design-to-metrology production line for metallic and freeform optics.
projects.Description:
A 5-axis single-point diamond-turning machine in a temperature-controlled enclosure, 3D surface profilers, a cryo-cycling chamber, and an ultra-precision CMM. The production line Design → CNC → polishing → SPDT → metrology has reached TRL 6.

FY68 delivered the SPDT machine, profilers, cryo-chamber, and a TRL-4 production line; FY69 added the metrology upgrade (ultra-precision CMM, surface-quality tester, vacuum oven); FY70 proposes a surface-verification system (dual-mode laser interferometer, high-power microscope) and environmental control.
projects.Facility / telescope: 5-axis SPDT machine; 3D surface profilers; cryo-cycling chamber; ultra-precision CMM

projects.One-line summary *: Mission simulations and mock observations for ESA's ARRAKIHS dark-matter space telescope; NARIT is the first Thai institute in an approved ESA mission.
projects.Description:
NARIT's simulation-software development for ARRAKIHS began in 2018, and the institute is represented in the mission consortium by the team PI. NARIT's CHALAWAN cluster is one of four computing systems supporting mission simulations worldwide; the mock observations also yield cosmological dN/dz science from background galaxies.

The mission was adopted by ESA's Science Programme Committee on 10–11 June 2026, with launch planned for late 2030.
projects.Key numbers: ESA F-class mission; launch planned late 2030

projects.Project name *: Photometric reverberation mapping of a z = 0.535 AGN in MACS J1149
projects.One-line summary *: Multi-band (ugriz) monitoring of an AGN behind the galaxy cluster MACS J1149 with ULTRASPEC on the 2.4-m TNT to measure time lags and infer the black-hole mass.
projects.Description: A 2020 ugriz monitoring campaign with ULTRASPEC on the 2.4-m Thai National Telescope. The analysis combines a PSF/aperture photometry pipeline with ICCF, JAVELIN, and Gaussian-process lag analysis, leading to a black-hole mass inference. Manuscript in preparation for ApJ.

projects.Project name *: Low-Resolution Spectrograph for the 2.4-m Thai National Telescope
projects.One-line summary *: Interchangeable long-slit spectrograph for the 2.4-m TNT with on-the-fly slit change, a high-resolution VPH grating, and an off-axis pick-off mirror for guiding.
projects.Description: The LRS reached r' = 19.5 mag in 15 min in its latest on-sky test on the TNT. A user-friendly GUI and packaged reduction routines are in development. The prototype, installed in December 2018, delivered R ≈ 800–1,300 over 440–740 nm (Paenoi et al. 2019).

projects.Project name *: Machine-learning parameter extraction for high-redshift galaxies
projects.One-line summary *: Machine-learning inference of physical properties and redshift classes of JWST-era high-redshift galaxies from photometry and imaging.

projects.Project name *: Compact H II galaxies with GTC/MEGARA
projects.One-line summary *: Spatially resolved IFU spectroscopy of local luminous compact blue galaxies as low-redshift analogs of high-redshift galaxies and as cosmic distance indicators.
projects.Description: MEGARA/GTC IFU spectroscopy of 26 local LCBGs shows that a kinematic correction for non-Gaussian line profiles reduces the scatter of the L(Hβ)–σ relation from 0.28 to 0.22 dex (Camazón-Pinilla, Guzmán & Chanchaiworawit, A&A submitted 2026).

projects.Project name *: Bursty star formation at z > 6 in the JWST era
projects.One-line summary *: How large-scale structure formation enhances or quenches star formation on the main sequence at z > 6, toward the epoch of first assembly and reionization.

projects.Project name *: Ensemble AGN variability in SDSS DR17
projects.One-line summary *: Ensemble structure functions of intrinsically low-luminosity AGN at z < 0.84 from PCA-decomposed SDSS spectra (Chanchaiworawit & Sarajedini, ApJ 2024).
Discovery and spectroscopic confirmation of a Coma-analog protocluster of Lyman-α emitters at z = 6.5 with the 10.4-m GTC (OSIRIS imaging and multi-object spectroscopy).
projects.Description: About 45 h of OSIRIS imaging to 26.5 mag (AB) and 42 h of multi-object spectroscopy on the GTC (≈ 87 h in total) revealed an overdense region of Lyman-α emitters at z = 6.5, confirmed spectroscopically and characterized as a Coma-analog protocluster (MNRAS 2017; ApJ 2019; MNRAS 2019; MNRAS Letters 2020).

news.Text *: The first independent SEA OtTeRS and SEAL Lab website are live. Now, with various goals, we share one home online.

SEAL Lab hosts the Southeast Asia Single-Point Diamond Turning and Reflective-Optics Capability conference on Sep 15–18, 2026, at the Kantary Hills Hotel, Chiang Mai, chaired by Krittapas Chanchaiworawit.

ESA's Science Programme Committee adopted ARRAKIHS at its meeting on 10–11 June 2026, with launch planned for late 2030. NARIT, a member of the mission consortium, contributes mission simulations on its CHALAWAN cluster.
The week-long school ran Apr 27–May 1, 2026, at the Kantary Hills Hotel, Chiang Mai, chaired by Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Supaluck Chanthawan, and Matipon Tangmatitham.
The Thailand–UK Python+Astronomy Summer School 2025 ran Oct 6–10, 2025, at the Kantary Hills Hotel, Chiang Mai.

team.Team tagline (one sentence): From the observed sky to the instruments that make it work.
team.Team intro paragraph: Our team consists of young, multi-discipline personnels--astronomer/astrophysicist, research assistants, optomechanical engineers, mechanical engineers, and full-stack developers. We are attacking challenges in astronomical research on two fronts--novel research methods and cutting-edge instrumentation technology.
team.SEA OtTeRS – intro paragraph: We pool access to small- to world-class telescopes to explore how the Universe has evolved and how it has influenced interactions with its large-scale structure and galaxies. The observations are made through redshift surveys and time-domain monitoring to peer into the ever-changing nature of galaxies and active galactic nuclei. Machine Learning techniques and Artificial Intelligence are used to aid in extracting hidden parameters and information where the data are sparse or incomplete. At the same time, we are building all-in-house low-resolution spectrographs for the 2.4-m and 0.7-m telescopes with robotic capabilities to seve as the workhorse for spectroscopic follow up of transients and time-domain events in Thailand.
team.SEAL Lab – intro paragraph: The team is spearheading the development of manufacturing capabilities for metallic optics for astronomical and space instruments, with the first and most complex 5-axis ultra-precision single-point diamond-turning facilities in Southeast Asia. Partnering with world-class research institutes in the UK and the US, we transfer and localize technologies in machining and manufacturing freeform optics for astronomical uses and space missions. We aim to be the regional leader in ultra-precision (nanometer-scale) metallic reflective optics for both astronomical instrumentation and industrial solutions.
team.Other telescopes / facilities to name: 2.4-m Thai National Telescope (TNT); 0.7-m Thai Robotic Telescope (TRT); 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC)
